Cerebral

/suh-REE-bruhl/ - the stress falls on REE · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Cerebral means ruled by or appealing to the mind rather than the emotions.

The station's new quiz show is proudly cerebral — no buzzers, no confetti, just four strangers reasoning aloud.

Worked Example

The trio's third album puzzled the club owners who booked them. Every track is built on interlocking time signatures, borrowings from Bach, and a drum line that answers the bass like a proof unfolding. Critics adored it. Dancers stood still. One review settled the matter in a phrase: this is cerebral jazz, music for the front of the skull.

Cerebral is the exact word because the album is related to the intellect — it appeals to the mind rather than the emotions. Plenty of music is clever underneath and still moves your feet; this music asks you to sit down and think. When a work's pleasures are ideas first and feelings second, cerebral names it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

intellectual: An intellectual loves ideas across the board — books, arguments, theories — and the word is broad and warm, saying nothing against the rest of the person. Cerebral is narrower and cooler: it claims the mind doesn't just lead but crowds the feelings out, in a person or in a work.

brainy: Brainy is the informal word for sheer cleverness — quiz-acing, puzzle-cracking mental horsepower. It measures how fast a mind runs, not where it lives. Cerebral is the temperament word: head over heart, ideas ahead of feelings, whatever the speed of the machinery.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

emotional: led and moved by feeling

gut-level: felt in the body before the mind can vote

Where it sits · how fully ideas crowd out feeling — thoughtful → cerebral → academic

thoughtful vs. cerebral: A thoughtful film has ideas in it somewhere; a cerebral one is built of ideas, aimed at the mind rather than the emotions.

academic vs. cerebral: Academic goes past cerebral — out of the concert hall entirely and into the seminar room, where footnotes outnumber feelings.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cerebr

Root — cerebr: brain (Latin cerebrum)

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Cerebr- (brain) + -al (relating to) = relating to the brain. Latin cerebrum is still the anatomist's name for the brain's great upper mass, the part that reasons. Call a film cerebral and you are saying, almost literally, that it lives in that organ — made for the brain, not the pulse.

Use the root in a new word: cerebrum

Use the root in a new word: cerebrum: Reasoning, language, and planning all run through the cerebrum, the brain's large upper region.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / critical

Cerebral is a reviewer's word: it praises — or gently warns — that a work appeals to the mind rather than the emotions. Call a person cerebral and you're saying they live in their head. Brainy is the informal cousin; intellectual is broader and warmer. Keep cerebral for head-over-heart, and note the faint chill it carries: what it gives the mind it often denies the pulse.
